correctness.rationale: The stated toric positroid is a parallel extension of U_(r,r+1). On a Pluecker chart omitting block k, monomial coordinate ratios split into independent smooth coordinates u_(j,s) and a_k by r matrix z_(s,i) of rank <=1. Its kernel is exactly the prime 2-minor ideal of the Segre cone, giving a scheme-theoretic affine chart A^(N-a_k-r) x D_(a_k,r), and the charts cover. The zero matrix gives precisely S_k. The Segre degree is binom(a_k+r-2,a_k-1), verified independently using Hilbert-polynomial top differences at (a_k,r)=(2,3),(3,3),(2,4),(4,4). The local divisor class group Pic(P^(a_k-1)xP^(r-1))/Z O(1,1) is Z; the canonical class (a_k-r) is torsion iff a_k=r, while a_k=1 is smooth. The global Q-Gorenstein/Gorenstein equivalence follows since each chart is normal Cohen-Macaulay. r>=3 and all a_k>=1; reduced singular support only.
